9. X’s stint as an aviator is one of the most fascinating "side quests" in history. While we think of him as a ______, in 1909 and 1910, he was obsessed with becoming the "King of the Air.” X wanted to be the first at everything and aviation was the "space race" of 1910. During his European tours, X realized that as a _______, he was often searched by customs. He theorized that if he could fly his own plane from country to country, he could bypass border checkpoints entirely. In March 1910, X took his plane to Diggers Rest, Victoria, Australia. At the time, no one had successfully performed a controlled flight in Australia. He had his name—X—painted in large block letters across the tail and the side panels and plucked the “fame out of thin air” like his well known profession. Id X.
